units.text: INT. EARNEST - CONTINUOUS
It’s pleasant, is it not, to see so perfect a reconciliation? I think we might leave the two brothers together.
units.name: CHASUBLE

units.text: Cecily, you will come with us.
units.name: MISS PRISM

units.text: Certainly, Miss Prism. My little task of reconciliation is over.
units.name: CECILY

units.text: You have done a beautiful action to-day, dear child.
units.name: CHASUBLE

units.text: We must not be premature in our judgments.
units.name: MISS PRISM

units.text: I feel very happy.
units.name: CECILY

units.text: They all go off except Jack and Algernon.
You young scoundrel, Algy, you must get out of this place as soon as possible. I don’t allow any Bunburying here.
units.name: JACK

units.text: Enter Merriman.
I have put Mr. Ernest’s things in the room next to yours, sir. I suppose that is all right?
units.name: MERRIMAN

units.text: What?
units.name: JACK

units.text: Mr. Ernest’s luggage, sir. I have unpacked it and put it in the room next to your own.
units.name: MERRIMAN

units.text: His luggage?
units.name: JACK

units.text: Yes, sir. Three portmanteaus, a dressing-case, two hat-boxes, and a large luncheon-basket.
units.name: MERRIMAN

units.text: I am afraid I can’t stay more than a week this time.
units.name: ALGERNON

units.text: Merriman, order the dog-cart at once. Mr. Ernest has been suddenly called back to town.
units.name: JACK

units.text: Yes, sir.
units.name: MERRIMAN

units.text: Goes back into the house.
What a fearful liar you are, Jack. I have not been called back to town at all.
units.name: ALGERNON

units.text: Yes, you have.
units.name: JACK

units.text: I haven’t heard any one call me.
units.name: ALGERNON

units.text: Your duty as a gentleman calls you back.
units.name: JACK

units.text: My duty as a gentleman has never interfered with my pleasures in the smallest degree.
units.name: ALGERNON

units.text: I can quite understand that.
units.name: JACK

units.text: Well, Cecily is a darling.
units.name: ALGERNON

units.text: You are not to talk of Miss Cardew like that. I don’t like it.
units.name: JACK

units.text: Well, I don’t like your clothes. You look perfectly ridiculous in them. Why on earth don’t you go up and change? It is perfectly childish to be in deep mourning for a man who is actually staying for a whole week with you in your house as a guest. I call it grotesque.
units.name: ALGERNON

units.text: You are certainly not staying with me for a whole week as a guest or anything else. You have got to leave . . . by the four-five train.
units.name: JACK

units.text: I certainly won’t leave you so long as you are in mourning. It would be most unfriendly. If I were in mourning you would stay with me, I suppose. I should think it very unkind if you didn’t.
units.name: ALGERNON

units.text: Well, will you go if I change my clothes?
units.name: JACK

units.text: Yes, if you are not too long. I never saw anybody take so long to dress, and with such little result.
units.name: ALGERNON

units.text: Well, at any rate, that is better than being always over-dressed as you are.
units.name: JACK

units.text: If I am occasionally a little over-dressed, I make up for it by being always immensely over-educated.
units.name: ALGERNON

units.text: Your vanity is ridiculous, your conduct an outrage, and your presence in my garden utterly absurd. However, you have got to catch the four-five, and I hope you will have a pleasant journey back to town. This Bunburying, as you call it, has not been a great success for you.
units.name: JACK

units.text: Goes into the house.
I think it has been a great success. I’m in love with Cecily, and that is everything.
units.name: ALGERNON

units.text: [Enter Cecily at the back of the garden.
She picks up the can and begins to water the flowers.] But I must see her before I go, and make arrangements for another Bunbury.
Ah, there she is.
Oh, I merely came back to water the roses. I thought you were with Uncle Jack.
units.name: CECILY

units.text: He’s gone to order the dog-cart for me.
units.name: ALGERNON

units.text: Oh, is he going to take you for a nice drive?
units.name: CECILY

units.text: He’s going to send me away.
units.name: ALGERNON

units.text: Then have we got to part?
units.name: CECILY

units.text: I am afraid so. It’s a very painful parting.
units.name: ALGERNON

units.text: It is always painful to part from people whom one has known for a very brief space of time. The absence of old friends one can endure with equanimity. But even a momentary separation from anyone to whom one has just been introduced is almost unbearable.
units.name: CECILY

units.text: Thank you.
units.name: ALGERNON
